Shed 4 reported approximately 4.8 inches of snow depth increase. It reported 1.3 inches from 7 to 8 am.

Starting at 11:15 AM_ the precipitation sensor was detected and live webcams showed precipitation increasing from the west. Road surface temperatures were recorded to be between 25 degrees at the start and 23 degrees by 12:30 PM. Wind gusts were between 10 mph and 23 mph from 11:15 AM to 12:30 PM. MDT 15 minute webcam imagery showed near zero visibility between 12 PM and 1 PM. Precipitation sensor stopped reporting activity at 12:45 PM and webcam imagery showed visibility improvement after 1 PM MST.

The sensor at Marias Pass received 0.51 of liquid which could equate to 6 to 8 inches of snowfall.

Light snow started at the airport at 11:30 AM. Visibility quickly reduced down to 0.75 miles in 9 minutes. ASOS reported winds gusting between 35 and 39 mph. Moderate snow fall by the ASOS was reported between 11:45 and 11:55 AM with visibility down to 0.5 miles. Visibility improved to over 1 mile after 11:55 AM. Airport staff called at 11:45 AM with 0.8 inches of new snow at the airport from the snow squall that passed through and near zero visibility. FAA Webcam 15 minute imagery showed the reduction in visibility of less than a quarter of a mile.

At 11:35 AM_ Three Forks AWOS reported wind speeds sustained at 40 mph and gusts at 52 mph. These conditions continued until 12:15 PM. METAR observation at 12:55 PM reported visibility down to 0.25 miles and haze conditions. FAA webcam imagery between 11:45 AM and 12:30 PM showed snow falling with less than a quarter mile of visibility. Visibility improved to 7 miles at the 1:55 PM METAR observation.
